reason: The passage depicts leaders (the princes/נשיאים) and the people (the congregation/עדה) working together, though within a hierarchical structure. After the discovery of the Gibeonite deception, the congregation complains to the leaders (וַיִּלֹּ֥נוּ כָל־ הָעֵדָ֖ה עַל־ הַנְּשִׂיאִֽים). The leaders respond by defending their oath and explaining their position, effectively addressing the people's concerns. Subsequently, they jointly execute the covenant terms, with the people/congregation collectively implementing the arrangement whereby the Gibeonites become 'wood-cutters and water-carriers for the congregation' (חֹטְבֵ֥י עֵצִ֛ים וְשֹׁ֥אֲבֵי מַ֖יִם לָֽעֵדָ֑ה). Joshua, as leader, and the Israelite community cooperatively ensure the covenant is honored and the decision is implemented.
